original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Does research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py return the same 8-word P112 set on the 36-generator basis whose positive-word SHA256 is ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3? The named batch size is 20, and every other legal batch size is included because the refusal happens before the lane split.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured speedup that keeps coverage. Priority revision 8 says faster output is equivalent coverage only after the sets are compared. Open PR #7007 records this 8-word hash and leaves the intersection-counter engine unrun. This package runs that engine on the recorded 36-generator basis. It records no timing and leaves the selected conditional exponent unchanged.
bottleneck_link: A faster iterator can certify a code only when it returns that code's low-weight words. On this 36-generator basis the opt-in engine refuses the input, so it does not supply those words. The selected conditional exponent is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop after the engine call on this 36-generator basis. Do not edit the frozen engine, enumerate the 2^36 code, time either iterator, or compare the E6 or D6 support sets.
evidence: The rebuilt kernel basis has the pinned free coordinates, weights, and generator-list SHA256 c93a6ec3f6d61b3bbf4086218c723761e517bc42ac2c26f551436d271a081e9d. The seven partition supports have SHA256 ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3. low_weight_words raises ValueError dimension exceeds 27 with zero yields at each batch size 1..20. Batch size 20 is the only legal size for which the later batch-count guard would admit 36 generators, and the observed message is still the dimension guard. The ordered 27-prefix is admitted and its span misses four of the seven supports. No codeword enumeration was run.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: If an opt-in copy raises only the dimension guard from 27 to 36, does batch size 20 on this same basis yield the eight-word set with hash ff8861dab18040c03d403a860773218df7c120d03770d701afb61b78c941e3d3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The published engine stops before the lane loop, so this refusal does not say whether the intersection arithmetic agrees with the recorded set.
open_questions.first_step: Leave research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py unchanged. In a separate harness, admit dimension 36 at batch size 20 and compare the yielded set with this hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: That comparison is a 36-dimensional stream. This package stops at the published guard and does not modify the frozen engine.

open_questions.question: Does some other independent generating set of length at most 27, still inside this code, make the same engine return these eight words at batch size 20?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cap rejects every 36-generator input. The seven supports span only seven dimensions, so a shorter admissible generating set is a different question from truncating this ordered basis.
open_questions.first_step: Name 27 independent generators of a subspace that contains all seven supports, call low_weight_words once at batch size 20, and compare the yielded set with this hash.
open_questions.blocked_by: The ordered 27-prefix of this basis misses four supports, and this package does not search another generating set. The 2^36 census that identifies the eight words remains PR #7007.
